newsitem.title: JAPAN: Europe central banks may sell more gold - Rothschild.
newsitem.headline: Europe central banks may sell more gold - Rothschild.

text.p: European central banks may sell more of their gold holdings in the future, amid pressure to reduce budget deficits as European monetary union proceeds, Robert Guy, director of N.M. Rothschild, said on Friday.
Speaking at a Nikkei Gold Conference, Guy also said he expected stepped-up and more prudent central bank use of the gold lending and options markets.

Noting that Belgium's central bank has sold 700 tonnes of its gold in recent years, Guy told the gold industry conference: "I anticipate other central banks in Europe will seek and receive permission for gold sales...should there appear to be no other way in reducing the size of that member state's budget deficit."
He added that central banks would continue seeking to add value to their existing gold reserves.
He cited estimates by various market watchers that gold lending by central banks rose to 1,900 to 2,100 tonnes this year from 1,500 to 1,800 tonnes last year.

Pointing to explosive growth in options market activity by central banks, he said there had been fears that some central banks would be unable to buy back call options or meet deliveries on them if there was a sudden surge in the gold price.

"Some central banks do indeed appear occasionally to have mismanaged their positions, but it would seem that the lessons have been learned, fingers crossed, and the market continues to grow," he said.

He also said that, in the future, central banks might start lending out their gold for longer periods, while growth in off balance sheet activity could switch from options to forward rate agreements and interest rate swaps.
